results.title: Louisville Metro KY - Five (5) Years of Disposition Data for the Louisville and Jefferson County Landbank Authority, Inc.
results.description:
The Office of Housing & Community Development Focuses on the full range of land development activities, including vacant property initiatives, housing & community development programs.
Data Dictionary:

“LBA” is the abbreviation for the Louisville and Jefferson County LBA Authority, Inc.
"Parcel ID" is an identification code assigned to a piece of real estate by the Jefferson County Property Valuation Administration. The Parcel ID is used for record keeping and tax purposes.
“IMPROV” stands for whether or not the real estate parcel had an “improvement” (i.e., a structure) situated on it at the time it was sold. “1” indicates that a structure existed when the parcel was sold and “0” indicates that the parcel was an empty, piece of land.
“APPLICANT” is the individual(s) or active business entity that submitted an Application to Purchase the real estate parcel and whose application was presented to and approved by the LBA’s Board of Directors. The Board of Directors must approve each application before a transfer deed is officially recorded with the Office of the County Clerk of Jefferson County, Kentucky.
“SALE DATE” is the date that the Applicant signed the transfer deed for the respective real estate parcel.
“SALE AMOUNT” is the amount that the Applicant paid to purchase the respective real estate parcel.
“SALE PROGRAM” is the LBA’s disposition program that the Applicant participated in to acquire the real estate parcel.

The Office of Community Development defines each “Sale Program” as follows:

  • Budget Rate (“Budget Rate Policy for New Construction Projects”) – Applicant submitted a proposed construction project for the empty, piece of land.
  • Cut It Keep It - Applicant requested to maintain the empty piece of land situated on the same block as a real estate parcel owned by the Applicant. Applicant must retain ownership of the lot for three (3) years before the Applicant can sell it.
  • Demo for Deed (“Last Look – Demo for Deed”) – Applicant requested to demolish the structure situated on the real estate parcel and retain the land for a future use.
  • Flex Rate (“Flex Rate Policy for New Construction Projects”) – Applicant submitted a proposed construction project for the empty, piece of land but did not have proof of funding or a timeline as to when the project would be completed.
  • Metro Redevelopment – The real estate parcel was part of a redevelopment project being considered by Metro Government.
  • Minimum Pricing Policy – The pricing policy that was approved by the LBA’s Board of Directors and in effect as of the real estate parcel’s sale date.
  • RFP (“Request for Proposals”) - Applicant requested to rehabilitate the structure in order to place it back into productive use within the neighborhood.
  • Save the Structure (“Last Look – Save the Structure”) - Applicant requested to rehabilitate the structure in order to place it back into productive use within the neighborhood.
  • Side Yard – The Applicant requested to acquire the LBA’s adjoining piece of land to make the Applicant’s occupied, real estate parcel larger and more valuable.
  • SOI (“Solicitation of Interest”) – The LBA assembled two (2) or more real estate parcels and the Applicant submitted a redevelopment project for the subject parcels.

For more information about each of the current disposition programs that the LBA offers, please refer to the following website pages:

https://louisvilleky.gov/government/community-development/vacant-lot-sales-programs
https://louisvilleky.gov/government/community-development/vacant-structures-sale

Contact:

Connie Sutton

connie.sutton@louisvilleky.gov

results.name: Join_Features_to_Address_-_View
results.title: Join - Address - View
results.description:
The Jefferson County Address Points layer contains authoritative site address locations maintained for properties and structures throughout Jefferson County, Idaho.

This dataset is a foundational component of the County's geographic information system and supports a wide range of governmental and public uses. Address information is used in support of 911 and emergency response, property assessment, planning and zoning, public notification and mailing processes, election address validation, mapping, navigation, and other administrative functions. Address information may also be used by utilities, delivery services, businesses, and the general public for location and reference purposes.

Address points generally represent assigned physical addresses and may include components such as house number, street name, directional prefixes or suffixes, street type, unit or subaddress information, jurisdiction, postal information, and other attributes used to identify and locate an address.

Jefferson County maintains and updates this dataset as addresses are assigned, corrected, or otherwise modified. Although the County strives to maintain accurate and current information, discrepancies may exist due to ongoing development, construction, addressing changes, field conditions, data processing, or differences between County records and information maintained by other agencies or service providers.

This layer should be considered the authoritative Jefferson County GIS source for County-maintained addressing information.
results.snippet: Authoritative address point locations for Jefferson County, Idaho, supporting public safety, property administration, planning, elections, navigation, delivery, and other location-based services.

Jefferson County makes reasonable efforts to maintain accurate and current addressing information; however, the County makes no warranties, expressed or implied, regarding the completeness, accuracy, positional accuracy, currency, reliability, or suitability of this dataset for any particular purpose.

Address locations and attributes may change as new addresses are assigned, development occurs, errors are corrected, or information is updated. Users should not assume that an address point represents a surveyed location, property boundary, legal description, ownership determination, or precise structure entrance.

This dataset may support emergency response and other public-safety operations; however, public access to this layer does not constitute or replace official emergency dispatch systems, procedures, or records. Users should not rely solely upon this public dataset for emergency response, life-safety decisions, or other applications requiring independently verified location information.

For applications requiring current or authoritative addressing information, users should obtain the most recent information available from Jefferson County.

results.name: NYS_Septic_Replacement_Grant_Round_5___Eligibility_Map_WFL1
results.title: NYS Septic Replacement Grant Round 5 _ Eligibility Map_WFL1
results.description:
This web map displays tax parcel boundaries, their municipalities, and their corresponding 250-foot buffer zones within Jefferson County, New York, created for the NYS Septic System Replacement Fund Program (Round 5).

Key Data Features & Sources:
- Priority Buffers: 250-foot spatial buffer zones surrounding designated WI/PWL priority waterbody segments.
- Parcel Screening: County tax parcel boundaries linked with NYS Environmental Facilities Corporation (EFC) and DEC grant eligibility criteria.

-Municipal Boundaries: Town and village boundaries for Jefferson County, NY 

Target Audience: Jefferson County property owners, county health and planning staff, local contractors, and environmental officials.
results.snippet:
Interactive web map showing property parcel eligibility within Jefferson County for the New York State Septic System Replacement Fund Program (Round 5). Use this map to check if a property falls within the designated 250-foot priority waterbody buffer zone.

Disclaimer: This map is intended for preliminary screening purposes only based on county GIS data. Final grant eligibility is subject to site verification and approval by county health/planning officials under NYS Environmental Facilities Corporation (EFC) program guidelines.
results.accessInformation: Real Property Tax Services GIS Division, Jefferson County, NY
results.licenseInfo:
This map is intended strictly for preliminary screening and planning purposes. Spatial boundaries, parcel inclusion, and waterbody features are derived from Jefferson County GIS parcel data and the NYS DEC Waterbody Inventory/Priority Waterbodies List (WI/PWL) layer.

Inclusion on this map or proximity to a mapped WI/PWL waterbody does not guarantee grant approval. Final eligibility determinations are subject to field verification, application review, and formal approval by Jefferson County health/planning officials under NYS EFC program guidelines.

results.name: Parcel_Boundaries_of_Indiana_Current
results.title: Parcel Boundaries of Indiana Current
results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. These layers include address points, street centerlines, land parcels, and governmental boundaries.
results.snippet:
This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

If attempting to download this data in shapefile or file geodatabase format on indianamap.org, please note that this dataset is too large to fit in a shapefile and generating a geodatabase does not perform well in the ArcGIS Hub interface. To download a pre-zipped file geodatabase, please go to https://countydataharvest.in.gov/statewide/2022/DataHarvest_2022_SingleFGDB_20230125.zip.
results.accessInformation: This data set was created as part of the Indiana Geographic Information Office's GIS Data Harvest Program. The source data used to create this dataset was provided by Indiana counties.
results.licenseInfo: CREDIT - It is requested, but not required, that the Indiana GIS Data Harvest Program be cited in any products generated from this data set. If citing, the following source citation language should be included: [Parcel Boundaries of Indiana 2021: Parcel Boundaries Maintained by County Agencies in Indiana, (Indiana Geographic Information Office, File Geodatabase, Polygon Feature Class), 20220201].
results.source: Megan R.L. Compton, Indiana Office of Technology, Indiana Geographic Information Officer
